title: Landing: main with uncommitted tracking edits aborts the ff-merge
lead: *Proposed.* Before the landing merges main into the slice branch, and again right before the fast-forward, ork checks the main checkout for uncommitted changes to files the slice branch changes. A change outside the tracking files stops the landing at once, before the merge-in and the re-check, with a one-line reason that names the files. A failed fast-forward also pauses with one line. What ork does with uncommitted tracking files (stop, commit or stash) waits on the owner (Open owner questions Q1 to Q7).
findings_note: Wave 6, 2026-11-02 (friction F40): S213 landing aborted with 'Your local changes would be overwritten by merge: .slicer/log.jsonl' because the owner-session filing of the S235 spec answer was uncommitted on main. Landing should check main for uncommitted tracking files before the ff-merge and either stop early with a one-line message that names the files, or have ork commit them. Which of the two is the owner's decision; interview before specifying. Related: S238 (merge-in commit by ork).
boundary: **Not in this slice:** stashing, resetting or checking out the owner's files (unless Q1 (c)); committing files outside the tracking set; holding slicer's write lock; changes to the handoff-mode ID done commit (land.go:74-85) or to merge-in conflict handling (S238); a TUI or status layout change (unless Q6 (b)).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Wave 6 (2026-11-02, friction F40, the item's findings): S213's landing paused at the fast-forward with git's "Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge: .slicer/log.jsonl", because a filing of the S235 spec answer was uncommitted on main. The orchestrator committed it by hand and retried. That commit is `7f920d1` "File S235 spec answer (slept time prints 1h03m)" with `.slicer/log.jsonl`, `.slicer/render/slices/S235.md` and `.slicer/slices/S235.json` (`git show --stat 7f920d1`).

What the code at HEAD of main shows (read 2026-11-03):

- `land` reads the base branch (`internal/engine/land.go:48-55`), merges it in when it moved (`mergeBaseIn`, `land.go:61`, which renders and runs the full re-check, `land.go:158-185`), and only then runs `git -C P merge --ff-only B` (`land.go:65`). Nothing looks at the main checkout's tree first. So a dirty main is found only after the merge-in and the re-check.
- A failed fast-forward pauses with `git merge --ff-only B: ` plus the clirun error, which is `CALL: exit N: STDERR` with git's stderr as is (`land.go:65-66`, `internal/clirun/clirun.go:79-88`). git's text is several lines. `ork status` prints the pause reason as the wait, then `; next: ork retry ID` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:1279-1292`). The file name is there, but inside git's multi-line text.
- git refuses only when a dirty path is one the fast-forward writes. Probe on 2026-11-03 in a scratch repo (under `.scratch/`, removed after the probe): with `.slicer/log.jsonl` changed on the branch and uncommitted on main, `git merge --ff-only` printed the error and aborted; with only another file dirty, it fast-forwarded and left that file modified. Each slicer write appends to `.slicer/log.jsonl` (as in `7f920d1`), and every slice branch carries such writes, so nearly any uncommitted tracking edit on main blocks every landing.
- Who leaves such edits on main: owner sessions that file items, and ork itself. ork's spec-check answers run `slicer edit --append` in the main checkout and stay uncommitted by design (`internal/engine/speccheck.go:444-448`, `docs/state.md:178-181`). Later-note filings run `slicer add`, `promote` and score writes there (`internal/engine/later.go:103`, `:117`, `:138`; `docs/design.md:363-369`). adj filings run in the main checkout too (`Engine.AdjRoot`, `internal/engine/engine.go:303-306`; `later.go:171`; `internal/engine/answer_adj.go:28`). None of these writes takes the landing lock (`land.go:35`). The S235 edit has the form that `answerSpecCheck` writes (`Owner decisions (DATE): QUESTION -> ANSWER.`, `speccheck.go:430-443`); whether ork or the owner session wrote it is not verified.
- ork already commits main-checkout tracking edits in one case. In `handoff` mode, after `slicer land`, it runs `git add -A -- .slicer` and `git commit -m "ID done" -- .slicer` (`land.go:74-85`). That commit takes every uncommitted `.slicer` change, the owner's included, and keeps staged files outside `.slicer` out (`TestLandTrackingCommitLeavesTheOwnersStagedFilesAlone`, `internal/engine/land_test.go:788`). The ork project runs `implement_finish` `done` (`slicer config implement_finish`), so that commit does not run here.
- Merge drivers: ork's clone configures `slicer-generated`, `slicer-index` and `slicer-relay-roles` (`git config --get-regexp '^merge\.'`). In the scratch probe, with `log.jsonl merge=union`, `git stash pop` after the fast-forward applied the stashed line after the branch's line, with no conflict.
- The relay contract's Land steps (`slicer ai relay`, Land 7 and 10) do not mention a dirty main; step 10 commits `.slicer` on main with the command `land` prints. slicer runs no git command and has no commit or stash step for this: `slicer --root ../slicer find` for `uncommitted`, `stash` and `commit tracking` lists nothing that covers it (s175, a hint to commit worktree handoff state, is retired). slicer offers no command to hold its write lock (`find lock` lists none).
- adj: `landing.dirty-main` and `landing.tracking-commit` are not found. `git.commit` (34) is decided "ork commits" for a passed slice; `landing.in-ork` (162) is decided. `docs/state.md:23-26` says nothing is written inside a project except what git and slicer write for a slice, and `docs/boundaries.md:85-93` lists the commits ork makes on main. A commit of edits ork did not make for this slice is a new boundary item.
- Matrix edits are left uncommitted by an owner decision of 2026-10-29 (as S261's spec cites it), so `.slicer/relay-roles.json` can hold a deliberate uncommitted edit.

This slice touches `internal/engine`: it is the one engine-class slice of its wave.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Group A, every answer, `internal/engine/landdirty_test.go`. `moveBase` stages with `git add -A` (`land_test.go:215-221`), so each test writes its dirty files in P after `moveBase`.

- TestLandStopsBeforeTheMergeWhenMainHasChangesTheSliceTouches: `env.moveBase("base.txt", "from main\n")`; the slice also changes `shared.txt` (`slice\n`); the main checkout has `shared.txt` = `owner\n`, uncommitted. After `env.approve()` the run is paused with `Pending{Kind: error, State: land}` and the reason `landing stopped: uncommitted changes in P to files the slice changes: shared.txt; commit or stash them` (P is the path). No `merge -m` in the worktree's git calls, `len(env.seen) == 0` (no re-check), no `slicer land`, main's tip is unchanged and `shared.txt` in P is still `owner\n`. Fails first: the run merges and re-checks, then pauses with git's multi-line text.
- TestLandDirtyStopNamesAtMostFiveFiles: seven such files `a.txt` to `g.txt` give `a.txt, b.txt, c.txt, d.txt, e.txt +2 more` in sorted order. Fails first: git's text.
- TestLandIgnoresUncommittedFilesTheSliceDoesNotTouch: P has `shared.txt` modified (the slice does not change it), an untracked `scratch.txt` and a staged `notes.txt`. The run is committed, main's tip is the slice branch tip, and `git status --porcelain` in P still shows exactly those three entries. Guard: it passes before the change; mutation-check it (an overlap that returns every dirty path turns it red) and say so in the report.
- TestLandPausesWhenTheFastForwardFails (existing, `land_test.go:719`, changed): the untracked `feature.txt` in P that the slice adds is now named by the early stop: reason as above with `feature.txt`; no `merge --ff-only` call; after the file is removed, `Retry` lands. Fails first: the reason is git's text.
- TestLandChecksMainAgainBeforeTheFastForward: `env.moveBase`; `env.beforeCheck` writes `shared.txt` = `owner\n` in P (the slice changes `shared.txt`). The run pauses with the dirty reason after a green re-check; main's tip is still the moved base; `LandRecheck` is false. After `git -C P checkout -- shared.txt`, `Retry` lands with no second re-check (`len(env.seen) == 1`). Fails first: the run pauses with git's multi-line text.
- TestLandFastForwardFailureIsOneLine: the `ff-fails` switch makes `merge --ff-only` exit 1 with `fatal: one` and `fatal: two` on two lines. The reason has no newline and starts with `git merge --ff-only S04: `. Fails first: the reason has a newline.
- TestLandDirtyCheckErrorPauses: `status-fails` set to P makes `git -C P status` exit 1. The run pauses with a reason that starts `git status: ` and no merge runs. Fails first: no status call, the run lands.

Group B, Q1 (b) with the recommended Q2 to Q5 (rewritten after the answers):

- TestLandCommitsUncommittedTrackingEditsFirst: main gets `.slicer/log.jsonl` (`a\n`) and `.slicer/.gitattributes` (`log.jsonl merge=union\n`) committed after the worktree exists; the slice appends `branch\n`; P appends `owner\n` uncommitted and has a staged `notes.txt`. The run is committed. Main's history has `Tracking edits on main before landing S04` holding only `.slicer/log.jsonl`; `main:.slicer/log.jsonl` holds `owner` and `branch` once each; `notes.txt` is still staged; one re-check ran and it saw that commit as main's tip. Fails first: the run pauses with git's text.
- TestLandTrackingCommitSkipsWhenTheSliceDoesNotTouchThem: an untracked `.slicer/slices/S99.json` in P that the slice does not touch is not committed and stays untracked; no tracking commit. Guard; mutation-check.
- TestLandMixedDirtyStopsAndCommitsNothing: dirty `.slicer/log.jsonl` and `shared.txt`, both changed by the slice: the run pauses naming `shared.txt` only, and main's tip is unchanged.
- TestLandDoesNotCommitConfigOrMatrixEdits: a dirty `.slicer/relay-roles.json` that the slice also changes stops the landing with the dirty reason naming it.
- TestLandTrackingCommitFailurePauses: the existing `commit-fails` switch (`land_test.go:49-51`) makes the tracking commit fail; the run pauses with one line starting `git commit: `; `Retry` lands.
- TestLandTrackingEditDuringTheRecheckGoesBackToTheMergeOnce: `env.beforeCheck` appends a line to `.slicer/log.jsonl` in P on the first check only. ork commits it, merges again and re-checks: two tracking commits, two re-checks, the run lands. A write on every check pauses with the dirty reason after the second re-check.

Group B under Q1 (a): one test, TestLandStopsBeforeTheMergeOnUncommittedTrackingEdits, as the first Group A test with `.slicer/log.jsonl`. Under Q1 (c): the stash tests are written after the answer.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Steps 2 to 5 and 7 do not depend on an answer. Step 6 waits on Q1 to Q5; step 4's tracking part waits on Q5.

1. Tests first from the failing list. Confirm each fails for the reason given; mutation-check the guards.
2. `internal/engine/landdirty.go`: `func (e *Engine) dirtyOverlap(ctx context.Context, P, base, B string) ([]string, error)` returns the sorted, unique paths in both `e.changedPaths(ctx, P)` (`filescope.go:36`; tracked changes, staged changes and untracked files, both sides of a rename) and `git -C P diff --name-only -z base...B` (a read through `gitRead`). `dirtyReason(P string, files []string) string` returns `landing stopped: uncommitted changes in P to files the slice changes: F1, F2 +N more; commit or stash them`, at most `maxConflictNames` names, folded with `oneLine`. ork never runs `git stash`, `git checkout` or `git reset` in P (unless Q1 (c)).
3. `land.go`, after the base read (`:55`) and before the `merged` check: call `dirtyOverlap`. An error pauses with `git status: ` or `git diff: ` and the error. A non-empty list pauses with `dirtyReason` (Q1 decides how tracking paths are treated). When the branch is already in the base (a retry after the fast-forward), the three-dot diff is empty and nothing stops.
4. `land.go`, after `mergeBaseIn` returns proceed and before `:65`: the same check again, for an edit made during the merge-in or the re-check. It pauses as in step 3 (Q5 decides tracking paths).
5. `land.go:65-66`: the fast-forward failure reason becomes `oneLine("git merge --ff-only " + B + ": " + errText(err))`.
6. Waits on Q1 to Q5. Under the recommended answers: split the list into tracking paths (`.slicer/` except `.slicer/config.json` and `.slicer/relay-roles.json`) and the rest. If the rest is non-empty, pause naming the rest and commit nothing. Otherwise run `git -C P add -A -- PATHS` and `git -C P commit -m "Tracking edits on main before landing ID" -- PATHS`, by name and never with a pathspec of `.`, as `land.go:79-82` does; a failure pauses with one line. The base then moved, so `mergeBaseIn` merges it in with slicer's merge drivers and re-checks; a conflict there is S238's pause. At step 4 the same commit runs once more and goes back to `mergeBaseIn`; a further overlap pauses. Record each git call in `writes[]` (`gitWrite`). Add an adj ask `landing.tracking-commit` with the owner's answer, and update `docs/boundaries.md:85-93` and `docs/state.md:23-26`.
7. Docs: `docs/design.md` Landing gets the check as a new first step (*proposed*, S254): the paths, the one-line reason, the two places it runs, that ork leaves the files alone, and the one-line fast-forward failure in step 2.
8. Do not change `mergeBaseIn`, `settleMerge`, the handoff-mode `ID done` commit (`land.go:74-85`), the slicer calls or the landing lock.
9. Add the `CHANGELOG.md` entry last, under `## Unreleased`, marked *proposed*: "Landing stops before the merge, with one line naming the files, when the main checkout has uncommitted changes to files the slice changes." (Extend it after Q1.)

Owner decisions: 2026-11-07 (interview). Q1: when main has uncommitted tracking edits, ork commits the tracking files before the landing merge (not stop, not stash). Check docs/boundaries.md first: if it says ork may not write tracking files, the owner must record that exception in adj before this is built. Share one overlap helper with S217; land S254 first.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`; `go vet ./...`; `gofmt -l .`; `slicer check`; `adj lint`.
- `go -C WORKTREE test -race -count=3 ./internal/engine -run 'Land'`.
- [HUMAN CHECK] [AFTER LAND] In a real wave, with an uncommitted edit on main to a file outside `.slicer` that the slice also changes, approve the slice: the run pauses within seconds, before any re-check, and `ork status` shows the one line and `next: ork retry RUN`.
- [HUMAN CHECK] [AFTER LAND] Under Q1 (b): with an uncommitted slicer filing on main (for example `slicer note` on another item), approve a slice: it lands, `git log` on main shows the tracking commit before the landing, and the filing is in main once.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch: "Landing checks the main checkout for uncommitted changes before it merges".

sections.heading: Open owner questions
sections.body:
Open owner questions from the 2026-11-03 spec drafting. Ask the owner before the relay starts; step 6, Group B and the docs boundary changes wait on these.

Q1 What ork does with uncommitted tracking edits the slice also changes.
Options: (a) stop early like any other file: the one-line pause; the owner commits by hand and runs `ork retry` (ork makes no new commits on main and puts nothing at risk; one hand step on every landing after any filing on main, ork's own spec answers and later filings included; this is wave 6's stop, only earlier and in one line); (b) ork commits them on main by pathspec before the merge-in (`git add -A -- PATHS`, `git commit -m MSG -- PATHS`, as the handoff commit does, `land.go:79-82`); the merge-in then merges them into the slice branch with slicer's merge drivers and the landing re-checks (no hand step; one more commit on main; a full re-check on every such landing, because the base moved; ork commits edits it did not make for this slice, including an owner filing half written at that moment, since no slicer lock is held; a new boundary item: an adj record, proposed key `landing.tracking-commit`, and changes to `docs/boundaries.md` and `docs/state.md`); (c) ork stashes them (`git stash push -- PATHS`, fast-forward, `slicer land`, `git stash pop`) (no commit and no extra re-check; the scratch probe shows `stash pop` used the union driver for `log.jsonl`; but a pop that conflicts, for example on a slice JSON both sides changed, which has no merge driver here, leaves conflict markers in the owner's main checkout and the edit in the stash; a crash between push and pop hides the owner's work in a stash; an owner write during the window makes the pop refuse; new untracked files need `-u`; ork must find its own stash on a retry).
Recommendation: (b). The edits are records written through slicer, often by ork itself; ork already commits `.slicer` on main in handoff mode; the merge drivers exist for this case; (c) puts the owner's uncommitted work at risk.
Waits: Implement step 6, Group B, `docs/boundaries.md`, `docs/state.md`.

Q2 Which paths are tracking files.
Options: (a) `.slicer/` except `.slicer/config.json` and `.slicer/relay-roles.json` (the files slicer writes for items, notes, the log, the index and the render; the two config files can hold a deliberate uncommitted owner edit, since matrix edits stay uncommitted (owner decision 2026-10-29, as S261 cites it), so they take the stop path); (b) all of `.slicer/` (simplest; would commit an uncommitted matrix or config change); (c) (a) plus the adj store (`decisions/` in ork) (covers ork's adj filings in the main checkout; ork does not know the store directory without reading adj's `.adjudicate.json`, which ork avoids today (`internal/adjcli/adjcli.go:164`), or hard-coding `decisions/`; adj records are new files with distinct names, so they rarely overlap a slice branch; `decisions/.adj.lock` is tracked (`git ls-files decisions`) and whether adj rewrites it was not checked).
Recommendation: (a). An overlapping adj file takes the stop path.
Waits: Q1 (b) or (c) only; `TestLandDoesNotCommitConfigOrMatrixEdits`.

Q3 When ork acts on tracking edits.
Options: (a) only when a dirty tracking path is one the slice branch changes (the fast-forward would refuse); other dirty tracking files stay as they are (fewest commits; no merge-in or re-check when none is needed); (b) whenever any tracking path in P is dirty (main is clean after every landing; commits unrelated filings in progress and forces a merge-in and a re-check). In practice both act on nearly every dirty filing, since each slicer write appends to `.slicer/log.jsonl`.
Recommendation: (a).
Waits: `TestLandTrackingCommitSkipsWhenTheSliceDoesNotTouchThem`.

Q4 The commit message under Q1 (b).
Options: (a) `Tracking edits on main before landing ID`; (b) `Commit tracking edits` with the file list in the body. The author is the main checkout's git user, as for ork's other commits, with no AI attribution.
Recommendation: (a).
Waits: Implement step 6.

Q5 A new overlapping tracking edit during the merge-in or the re-check (the check before the fast-forward).
Options: (a) pause with the one-line reason (simple; a hand step for edits made in those minutes); (b) under Q1 (b), commit it and go back to the merge-in once, as relay Land step 7 says for a main that moved; a further overlap pauses (no hand step in the common case; a second re-check costs minutes; the bound stops a loop with a busy owner session). Non-tracking files always pause.
Recommendation: (b) under Q1 (b); otherwise (a).
Waits: Implement steps 4 and 6, `TestLandTrackingEditDuringTheRecheckGoesBackToTheMergeOnce`.

Q6 What the owner sees.
Options: (a) a stop shows its reason in `ork status` and the TUI as any pause does (one line, then `; next: ork retry ID`, `internal/daemon/runs.go:1288-1292`); a tracking commit is silent, seen in `git log` and the run's `writes[]`, as S180's changelog merge is; (b) as (a), and a landed run's Recent row says `committed N tracking edits on main first` (a new record field or reason text; makes this a UI slice with a UI pass, r14).
Recommendation: (a). This slice then changes no `internal/cli` or `internal/tui` code.
Waits: Files.

Q7 Human check.
Options: (a) the two `[HUMAN CHECK] [AFTER LAND]` lines in Check; (b) none; the temp-repo tests cover it.
Recommendation: (a). The tests do not run slicer's real merge drivers or a live owner session writing during a landing.
Waits: Check.
